themes.consensus_view: Banks agree AI data center spending is still being funded at a huge scale, with hyperscalers leaning more on borrowed money, but they split on whether that spending peaks soon because of politics, financing strain and weak free cash flow.

Banks lean positive on stocks after the midterms because history shows gains in the following year and a divided Congress limits big policy swings, while TCW says the economy matters more than the vote and UBS says politics now drives the market.
Banks read the strong October jobs report as proof the US labor market is holding up, and none of them argue it is weakening, so the debate is how much that pushes the Fed toward another hike.
Every bank that took a position expects the Fed to raise interest rates again in December after the strong October jobs report, and none argued against it.

Most banks lean toward owning Treasuries and gilts and buying dips, with falling yields tied to the equity sell-off, but they split on whether the short end of the US curve should be owned or avoided.

Banks agree the Bank of England raised its policy rate by 25 basis points in November and most read it as a hawkish signal, but nobody has staked a directional view on where rates go next beyond a few peak-rate and inflation-peak forecasts.
